description: PyNE, the Nuclear Engineering Toolkit, aims to provide a common set of tools for nuclear science and engineering. The README read on 2026-09-26 describes a package built with Fortran and C++ compilers, CMake, NumPy, SciPy, Cython, HDF5 and PyTables, with optional links to MOAB, DAGMC and OpenMC, and points to pyne.io for examples and documentation and to a mailing list and GitHub for contributions. Coverage is general nuclear engineering utilities, not a plant or country. Access is by building from the GitHub source; the latest git tag seen was 0.7.8. The licence file, copyright 2011 to 2020 by the PyNE Development Team, is a two-clause BSD licence, so use is free. Caveats: installation needs a full compiled tool chain, and the copyright years in the licence end in 2020, so the pace of recent development was not confirmed. Simulation uses are preparing materials, nuclear data and input decks for transport and depletion codes in reactor and fuel cycle studies, as part of a physics toolchain behind digital twin work. Related records: model-openmc is an optional dependency of PyNE, model-njoy-nuclear-data-processing processes the nuclear data such tools read, and model-cyclus-nuclear-fuel-cycle-simulator covers fuel cycle scenarios.
